question: Can deep networks be trained with FP16 storage and arithmetic without losing accuracy or changing hyper-parameters?
hypothesis: Three techniques (FP32 master weights, loss scaling, FP32 accumulation) let FP16 training match FP32 accuracy.
contributions: Demonstration across CNNs, detection, speech, translation, language modeling, GAN

method.summary: Store weights, activations and gradients in FP16, keep an FP32 master weight copy for updates, scale the loss to keep small gradients representable, accumulate FP16 products in FP32. Compared against FP32 baselines on six task families with identical hyper-parameters.

datasets.name: ILSVRC12
datasets.preprocessing: Caffe: random horizontal flip and random crop from 256x256; Resnet50 full PyTorch augmentation

datasets.name: Pascal VOC 2007/2012
datasets.split: Faster-RCNN trained on VOC07 train; SSD on VOC07+12; test VOC07

models.name: DeepSpeech 2 English
models.architecture: 2 2D conv, 3 GRU layers, 1 row conv, CTC

models.name: bigLSTM
models.architecture: 2 layers of 8192 LSTM cells, projection to 1024-d embedding

models.name: GNMT-style seq2seq LSTM (TF tutorial)
models.architecture: 3 or 5 layers encoder and decoder, 1024 LSTM cells each, attention

models.name: CNNs: AlexNet, VGG-D, GoogLeNet, Inception v2, v3, pre-act Resnet-50; Faster-RCNN and SSD (VGG-16 backbone); DCGAN

training.optimizer: Nesterov SGD (speech, 20 epochs); SGD (translation); Adagrad (bigLSTM, 50 epochs); Adam (DCGAN, 100K iterations)
training.precision: FP16 storage for weights, activations, gradients; FP32 master weights; FP16 products accumulated in FP32; reductions (batch norm statistics, softmax) in FP32
training.hardware: Baseline on Maxwell or Pascal GPUs; mixed precision on Volta V100; speech MP emulated on Maxwell with FP16 storage only

other.loss_scale: constant, 8 to 32K; SSD 8, bigLSTM 128; many networks none
other.frameworks: Caffe modified for Volta TensorOps; PyTorch for Resnet50; TensorFlow for translation

eval.protocol: One run per configuration for most tables; translation shows three FP32 runs to expose run-to-run variance; GAN judged qualitatively.

results.claim: Weights, activations and gradients stored in FP16 nearly halve training memory; an FP32 master copy adds 50% to weight memory only.
results.setup: Section 3.1 argument; activations dominate memory so overall roughly halved. No byte-per-parameter or optimizer-state accounting.

results.claim: FP16 cannot represent magnitudes below 2^-24 (become zero); max FP16 value 65,504.
A weight update becomes zero if weight magnitude is at least 2048x the update (10-bit mantissa).
results.quote: at least 2048 times larger that of the weight update

limits: Does not count bytes per parameter or optimizer-state memory (no Adam moments); only states FP32 master copy adds 50% to weight memory.
Speedups only from DeepBench operations; full network speedups left to future work (early library versions).
Single runs mostly; translation shows large run-to-run variance.
Speech models trained in emulated mode (FP16 storage on Maxwell), and on internal data.
Uses FP16 with loss scaling; BF16 not discussed. Seeds, learning rates and batch sizes mostly unstated.
Dynamic loss scaling proposed as future work, not implemented.

terms.definition: scale the loss value computed in the forward pass prior to starting back-propagation so gradients shift into FP16 range; unscale weight gradients before the update
